title: Detecting isomorphisms on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring and $T$ a scheme. Use left module sheaves and the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. An isomorphism of complexes below means an isomorphism in the derived category, not a degreewise isomorphism of the chosen complexes.

1. **Locality for covering families.** A morphism $u:F\to G$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ is an isomorphism if and only if its inverse image along every member of one pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to T\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is an isomorphism. A complex is acyclic if and only if every cohomology sheaf vanishes; a sheaf vanishes if and only if its restrictions along the members of such a covering family vanish.
2. **Detection on the affine ind-etale basis.** If $T$ is affine, a sheaf $\mathcal H$ vanishes if and only if $\mathcal H(W)=0$ for every $W$ in the affine ind-etale basis [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Consequently $u$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for every integer $n$ and every such $W$, the map of sections of its cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(u)(W):\mathcal H^n(F)(W)\to\mathcal H^n(G)(W)$ is an isomorphism. For general $T$ use these bases over an affine open cover. No assertion is made that ordinary evaluation of an arbitrary complex on these basis objects preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
3. **Complexes of etale origin.** Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $v:F'\to G'$ be a morphism in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Then $\nu_T^*v$ is an isomorphism if and only if for every geometric point $\bar t$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$ its map on geometric stalks of cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism. Pro-etale geometric stalks are those of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. In particular they are jointly conservative on all morphisms between the bounded constructible objects $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, defined as objects of etale origin in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules].
4. **Warning about geometric points.** In general, geometric-point stalks are not conservative on all abelian sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, although the covering-family and basis criteria above remain valid there. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed and a nonzero abelian group $A$, let $\mathcal Q_A$ be the sheafified quotient of the sheaf of all set maps $|U|\to A$ by the constant abelian sheaf. On affine objects it has values $\mathcal Q_A(U)=\operatorname{Map}(|U|,A)/\operatorname{LC}(|U|,A)$, where locally constant means constant on an open neighbourhood of each point. Then $\mathcal Q_A(T)=0$ and all its geometric-point stalks are zero, but $\mathcal Q_A\ne0$.

proof.text: Use the proved upstream isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction to detect isomorphisms of underlying abelian sheaves on the covering family. Evaluate module slice restrictions on each over-object to supply its hypotheses, then reflect isomorphisms through SheafOfModules.toSheaf. Apply this criterion to the zero endomorphism to detect zero sheaves. For abelian sheaves apply the upstream criterion directly. Empty covering families are included.

proof.text: Slice restriction is additive sectionwise. Its existing left adjoint makes it preserve finite colimits. Its composite with the faithful module-presheaf forgetful functor is ordinary precomposition and preserves finite limits, so reflection of limits makes slice restriction left exact. Use the exact-functor homology natural isomorphism and DerivedCategory.isIso_iff to apply the covering criterion to every homology morphism. Acyclicity is exactness at each degree, equivalently zero homology.

source.place: Tag 0991, section-points; blueprint Proof Step 1, corrected derived-category interpretation

proof.text: For affine $T$, the cited basis theorem says restriction determines sheaves and detects their isomorphisms. Apply it to $0\to\mathcal H$ to obtain the asserted zero-sheaf criterion. A natural transformation between sheaves on the basis is invertible if and only if its component maps are invertible: the component inverses are natural by composing the original naturality equations with them. Apply this to each $\mathcal H^n(u)$, then the unbounded derived isomorphism criterion. For a general $T$, first restrict to every member of an affine open cover and apply clause (1), then apply the affine test on each member. This uses sections of cohomology sheaves, not cohomology of ordinary section complexes.

source.place: Proof Step 2, replacing the false ordinary-evaluation inference

proof.text: The coefficient realization followed by forgetting modules is naturally isomorphic to the original underlying abelian sheaf, using the sheafification counit. Forgetting fixed modules commutes with the pointed-neighbourhood colimit. Compose these natural isomorphisms with the canonical comparison-stalk isomorphism and the exact comparison functor homology isomorphism. This identifies the compared cohomology stalk maps with the underlying abelian etale stalk maps, for arbitrary finite rings.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale; Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point; corrected blueprint Proof Step 3

proof.text: Apply the proved etale geometric-stalk conservativity theorem to each homology map and reflect isomorphisms through forgetting modules. DerivedCategory.isIso_iff then makes the etale derived map invertible, hence its comparison invertible. Conversely any functor preserves isomorphisms. For arbitrary constructible morphisms choose the etale-origin presentations in their definition, use the lower homology bounds to regard them as bounded-below objects, lift the conjugated map using the full faithfulness theorem siteComparison_boundedBelow, and conjugate the result back.

source.place: Tag 0991, section-points; blueprint Proof Step 3, including arbitrary morphisms between constructible objects

proof.text: Use exists_proEtale_functions_quotient_sections to identify the all-functions presheaf with its functions sheaf, compatibly with constant functions. The sheafification counit and unit triangle identity identify the constructed cokernel with the lemma cokernel. The residue fields of Spec k are isomorphic to k, giving its affine section formula. All functions on Spec k are constant, so its quotient sections vanish. Apply the already proved classicalStalk_initial lifting-and-rigidity construction directly with R=k and j=identity. Its identity pointed neighbourhood is initial; its opposite is terminal and its colimit leg is an isomorphism. Thus all geometric stalks vanish, also over extension fields.

Let E be the one-point compactification of the universe-lifted discrete natural numbers and B=LocallyConstant E k. The proved source-library instance LocallyConstant.weaklyEtale makes Spec B an affine pro-etale object. LocallyConstant.homeomorphPrimeSpectrum identifies its points with E times the singleton Spec k. Choose nonzero a in A and the function equal to a at infinity and zero elsewhere. If locally constant, its zero fibre would be closed and contain the dense natural numbers, hence infinity, contradiction. Its affine quotient class is nonzero, so the quotient sheaf is nonzero. Direct weak etaleness avoids the filtered-presentation construction.
